criteria_note: Scored A-G, X1 and guide-specific T1-T3 (R*, U*, S1 do not apply). Claims checked against docs.ray.io/en/latest (Ray 2.60.0, fetched 2026-11-09) and Ray master source (serve/_private/replica.py, constants.py, scripts.py). Code was read, not executed. Prose length = body minus front matter, headings, fenced code, display math, tables, images and the Sources list. Means: X 7.91, Y 7.36.

A.reason: Opens with ## TL;DR (L11) and claim-shaped noun-phrase headings (L17, L142, L617, L1080); architecture right after concepts. Deductions: the install command is given twice (L92 'pip install "ray[serve]" transformers torch', L263 'pip install "ray[serve]"'); the MLflow __call__ excerpt L381-392 repeats L368-376 verbatim; the GCS section L1076-1078 is a heading plus one sentence.

B.reason: Natural 입니다 register, few formulaic sentences ('다음과 같습니다.' once). Deductions: terminology mixes an English noun with Korean particles while translating its sibling ('deployment는 Ray Serve의 중심 개념입니다' L55 vs '레플리카' L61; rewrite '디플로이먼트는...'); 'Deployment, replica, application: 스케일과 업그레이드의 세 단위' heading in mixed scripts (L49).

C.reason: Cross-references broken: L1070 '앞서 Translator에 추가한 `reconfigure` 경로로' refers to a reconfigure method the post never adds; L256 promises 'GCS 장애 허용 설정은 뒤의 KubeRay 섹션에서 다룹니다' but L1078 gives one sentence and no config; L719 starts a worked example ('예를 들어 ... `num_gpus: 0.0`만 적었다고 해 보겠습니다.') and never states the result. Otherwise the Translator→Summarizer running example threads the whole post (L57, L166, L218, L1039).

D.reason: Hard parts get worked examples at the point of use: power-of-two with A=3,B=1,C=5,D=2 (L182), 480/48/24 ratio arithmetic (L233), code-vs-config merge table (L713), backpressure 2x100=200 (L678). Minor over-explanation: '$$(5+1)\times 2 = 12$$' (L539).

E.reason: Eight relevant figures with Korean alt text and absolute URLs (architecture L152, autoscaling L216, dashboards L812-820), parameter/default tables (L657), failure table (L245), update table (L1032), ASCII request-path diagram (L168). Deduction: duplicated code excerpt L381-392; ASCII diagrams labelled illustrative but the first one (L27) adds little.

F.reason: 27 of 28 checked claims match the docs. One fabricated cross-reference that breaks the running example: L1070 '앞서 Translator에 추가한 `reconfigure` 경로로 레플리카 재시작 없이 반영되므로' while the config at L754 sets 'user_config: language: french' for a Translator without reconfigure (Ray raises 'user_config ... specified but deployment ... missing reconfigure method').

G.reason: description 125 chars, longer than title, opens with 'Ray Serve는', no numbers; use_math true with $$ at L539; fences have single-word info strings; no Liquid. Title carries a version ('Ray Serve 2.60'), which dates quickly.

X1.reason: Data-Architecture is a valid topic and fits a serving library; controlled tags Model-Serving and MLOps; specific tags (Deployment-Handle, Power-of-Two-Choices, KubeRay) name what the post covers.

T1.reason: Most code runs as written (L97-130, L270-306, L404-474, L557-594). Break: following the post, 'serve deploy serve_config.yaml' (L779) with 'user_config: language: french' (L754) fails because the post's Translator has no reconfigure, yet L783-804 shows HEALTHY. 'mv serve_quickstart_composed.py text_ml.py' (L730) is a reasonable bridge.

T2.reason: Covers concepts, request path, autoscaling, composition, config precedence, CLI/REST, KubeRay in a sensible order, all grounded. Thin or missing: HTTP guide features (streaming responses, cancellation, middlewares), monitoring metrics; GCS FT setup only named (L1078).

T3.reason: Explains internals and design reasons: controller/proxy/replica roles (L148), handle path skipping step 2 (L166), two autoscaling signals and why (L218), what GCS keeps vs loses (L243-250), in-place vs zero-downtime (L1032), alternatives table (L1090) and selection criteria (L1110). Deduction: 17/17 sources are official docs; no design write-ups or papers beyond the linked IEEE paper.

preference.reason: X has the guide shape the rubric asks for (TL;DR, claim headings, architecture at 13%, a closing selection-and-failure assessment, eight correct figures) and fewer factual errors (1/28 vs 2/31). Y is broader and more runnable in places (HTTP, cancellation, fault tolerance, monitoring with exact defaults) and cites some non-official sources, but it reads like the docs in order, has no TL;DR or closing judgement, lost every image including the architecture diagram, and inverts the serve run behaviour.
